TextEng: You look about you, suspicious, but see nothing.
A portal glows softly before you. You wonder where it leads.

This woman is the very picture of a seer. Her long dark hair is held in a tangled ponytail. She wears a set of blood-speckled grey robes, as tattered, torn, and frayed as her unfocused gaze. A collection of beads and baubles rests around her neck, making soft clicking sounds when she moves.
Either he owned little to begin with or this man was stripped of all he had.
A bloodied notebook containing ghastly anatomy diagrams.

For a woman so obviously unstable, she was able to be straightforward and meticulous, when called upon. This ledger is proof of that. It details the process of the surgery performed on slaves procured from one Ulan Aurintar from the Sea Market -- via Farasano Corano. The raw materials for worldwine were smuggled into the city *inside* the bodies of the slaves, then transported to Quillian at the now destroyed warehouse for processing.

A note is included that the "loss rate" of the slaves is "within acceptable parameters." It also notes that Ulan is upset that it is cutting into his profit margins and he has made noises about backing out but "it won't matter soon."

The ledger also details the street level operations run by a woman called Harasi who, along with her crew, were collecting, selling, and storing the worldwine itself. Aladara seems to think she is based out of the Soul Trade Inn, though seems mostly unconcerned with her operations.

Finally, there is angry note near the back of the ledger that reads: "Warehouse destroyed. Only acceptable alchemist missing or dead. Find a new blasted alchemist or the lady will be displeased!" It is underlined several times in what looks like blood. There are only blank pages thereafter.

A collection of hand-woven decorations adorn the wall, made from what looks like beads and small bones. Probably from an animal. Probably.
A painting depicting a scene from the Sea Market. The lower left of the frame is engraved with the words "From Teddy."
This stove is well used and immaculately clean. It's obviously cared for a great deal.

The merchant stands before you, all smiles and warmth shining in blind, white eyes. Were you to describe the broad shouldered human, it would be with the words: well kept. His short brown hair is cut to perfectly flow into his close trimmed beard. His clothes are immaculately put together, yet he wears them casually, almost effortlessly. No easy feat.

The half-elf clearly favors the elven side of his heritage. Tall and lithe, he doesn't move so much as glide, his long dark hair moving behind his as if trying to catch up. His attire favors the flashy in a low cut vest, billowy shirt, and equally billowy pants. His features, beautiful by nearly any race's standard, contain equal parts interested and amused at any given moment. His left eyebrow threatens to float off of his face at any given moment.

There is nothing special about this object.
Metal studs poke through the woodwork of this ornate chest. Judging by the fine craftsmanship, this strongbox appears to have been intended for public display.

This document, ratified in triplicate by the Fraternity of Order, details the sale of this warehouse to House Corano.
Nails, chains, and metal working hammers fill these crates, along with not a small number of manacles.
A detailed list of stock from a ship called "The Flesh Peddler." It lists the number of slaves, including condition and losses, along with a passenger manifesto and extra cargo information.
These bales of hay appear to be used to change out the bedding of the slaves. They seem to be unused and smell faintly of rot.
A pile of books, carelessly discarded.

Several entries fill this ledger in a loose, flowing hand.

One entry you see is a note Ulan wrote to himself. It mentions needing to use the secret door in the back of the warehouse more -- now that the Coranos are no longer "laundering" them, the slaves needed to be delivered directly to a woman named Aladara for "processing." He curses the hassle and lack of efficiency in the process of masking slaves as penitent to a "spiritual advisor."

Another entry details the difficulty of finding priests and healers in order to get the supplies into the slaves, largely without them knowing. He writes about how "these fools don't understand the lengths he has to go through to get the job done." What follows is a list of blackmail options and leverages that he planned to levy against the operation in order to increase his profit margin, due to Aladara's "prime world heavy handedness" and the slaves' lack of "re-sale" value after she was done with them. You note that his profit margins already seemed surprisingly high, thanks to a rather large share of worldwine revenue.

A woman named Harasi is mentioned in an entry detailing profit lines and a cost benefit analysis of no longer having the Coranos as part of the operation. Ulan writes that Harasi, the woman in charge of the street-level dealings, is horning in on several aspects of the operation and trying to "take a bigger piece of my pie." Ulan muses on whether or not to "cut her in on a larger slice" or "make the woman choke on it." No further pastry based metaphor, or information, is detailed.

This note and ledger detail that a woman named Kyla is sharing a portion of her profits with the owners of the Rooster's Roost in exchange for room, board, and a promise to always mention that they've never seen Kyla before in their lives if anyone asks. It looks like Kyla runs her whole section of her operation from the Roost. 

The ledger the note was attached to has a number of discrepancies in it, from recorded income totals to some weird changes in handwriting. It looks like someone is doctoring the ledger in order to skim off the top. No one has noticed, as it seems like they only pay attention to the bottom line. The only one who could benefit from such errors would be Kyla, who could use this to reduce what she pays to the owners of the Rooster's Roost.
A yellowed and stained signboard that reads "SEAT YOURSELF!"

This stout dwarf wears an expression that could break rocks and lesser men on her well lined face. Her plain house dress is layered with what may either be flour or dust, possibly both. She, like the loose bun she keeps on the top of her head, is otherwise well kept. The only otherwise outstanding feature is the collar around her neck, marking her for a slave.
A pile of books and documents.

This collection of documents includes the deed for a building in the North Market District being rented by one Aladara the Dreamer. It's notarized by the Fraternity of Order. Farasano Corano paid more for her building than you would likely see in a lifetime of adventuring.

These documents detail the deeds and ownership of several warehouses in the Sea Market district, including one rented out to a slaver named Ulan Aurintar. Attached are receipts for the purchase of a very large number of slaves from Ulan, including notes that reference to the quality of the slaves "post-recovery." It doesn't detail what they are recovering from.
Such a large pool of blood tells the tale of someone who put up one hell of a fight.
Among the wreckage is a decanter containing an alcohol that looks like liquid gold and smells about as expensive.
This box is filled with some very expensive and sweet smelling pipeweed.
One of the books details the theorized layout of the Inner and Outer planes.
This streaked blood and single footprint indicates that this was the point of entry for a single assassin. Chilling to think one person may have been responsible for all the death here.

This tiefling is adorned head to toe in fine black silks of every texture imaginable, offsetting the gold necklace and rings that serve as his accessories. His long face is crowned in two horns, which curl alongside his cheeks, framing an almost perpetual sneer. Everything about Ulan seems to be crafted specifically  to make sure those looking at him know that he believes he is better than whatever activity he is engaging in at the time.

Squat, round, and happy, Teddy is the very picture of halfling contentment. His features are round and his constant smile makes them even rounder. You feel like he must have been an adorable baby. He wears his servant's clothes with pride and keeps his curly brown hair well kept, as would be expected for his station.

Everything about Lucenna's appearance screams, "capable." The tall human woman wears her immaculate full mithril plate with the ease and comfort of a veteran soldier. A blue half cape is splashed across her back, cut by a prim blond ponytail. She leans on a halberd, her hand on the hilt of one of two daggers slung to her belt, a bemused expression on her soft but battleworn features.

A knife in human form, Harasi is one severe woman. Everything about her has an edge. The sharp cut of her long black hair is offset by the brown hue of her skin. She moves as smoothly and quietly as a blade clearing a scabbard in the dark. Her eyes are almost constantly narrowed at whatever she is looking at, as if she suspects the entire world of lying to her.

The gnome, Quilian, stands before you hunched over, the result of hours of work. His brown skin is covered in small patches of dirt and ash he absently wipes at. It doesn't help. Blue hair sticks out of his peaked cap, also patched with grime of an indeterminate nature. His belt is lashed with pouches and it seems the other clothes he wears, from his half robe to his vest to his belt, are made of pockets. He constantly looks around and you'd swear his image shimmers and wavers out of the corner of your eye.

A collection of hellish jet black spikes and horns that serves as Shylia's full plate looms over you. You presume Shylia, a gigantic, intimidating human is in there because you can feel her glaring at you, the room, and probably at someone two planes over. She grips a spiked chain so wicked looking that other spiked chains probably call it "Ma'am."

The half-orc in front of you is all muscles and glaring. His right good eye stares with a force, always taking in the scene. His perpetual frown is pierced by two short,  jutting tusks, one broken but completed with a golden cap etched with an orcish glyph. He has adorned himself with a cap, loose shirt, and vest. His hands are wrapped in fingerless leather gloves. You can see the knuckles seem to be a bit worn.
This dog is sniffing around and whining.  You assume he is looking for his owner in the place he last saw him.

This creature is a salamander, a type of fire elemental with the lower body of a serpent and the upper body of a man. He's wearing the heavy apron of a smith or mechanic, festooned with tools and scraps of metal off some infernal contraption, covered in grease and scars.

The woman at the bar sports the kind of slump that comes with exceptional boredom. Her demeanor is at counterpoint to her features as everything else about her says career officer. A well muscled form lays beneath layers of studded leather armor. The hands that hold her drink are well calloused, but kept. Her hair is pulled back into a tight tail which makes her features even sharper. A bored sigh can be heard escaping her lips at times.

Small and wiry, this person keeps a close eye on the goings-on around them, even as you approach. Black and purple leathers clad a body that seems ready to pounce or flee at any moment, and a well-crafted rapier hangs at their side.
Tall, strong, and intimidating, this woman looks like the perfect military mercenary -- and she'd have to be to have survived as a warrior this long in such an inhospitable locale.

Her flesh and very countenance tell the tale of countless battles fought on distant fields. He eyes are bloodshot and always seem on the verge of going wide and wild. She wears what would be described as the garb of a gladiator on countless planes and strides through the world as if it were her arena.
